extra.message: JWT verification falls back to the public constant 'support-desk-local-secret-key'. AuthModule uses the same fallback for signing. When JWT_SECRET is absent, an attacker can forge a token containing an existing administrator's ID and authenticate as that administrator.

Public registration assigns the supplied organizationId without checking an invitation or organization membership. Both portal onboarding methods also accept it. An attacker who knows another organization's ID can register into it and access its tickets and attachments through the organization-based authorization checks.

POST /api/auth/portal/onboard passes unauthenticated workRounds directly to bcrypt.hash. PortalOnboardDto applies only IsOptional to this field, with no upper bound. Requests using large valid costs can occupy the hashing workers for extended periods and deny service to registration and authentication.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Portal onboarding defaults to bcrypt cost 4, substantially below the costs used by the other registration methods. Accounts created through this public endpoint receive password hashes with insufficient computational protection against offline guessing.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: validateUser performs password verification without tracking or limiting failed attempts. The public login, workbench/resume, and workbench/elevate routes call it without a throttling guard, enabling unrestricted online password guessing.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: RegisterDto validates password only with IsString, so an empty string passes server validation and is hashed by register(). Login likewise accepts an empty string. Direct API requests bypass the frontend minimum-length check and can create accounts with empty passwords.

PATCH /api/users/:id/profile-submission checks only that the caller owns the profile, merges the unrestricted body into the user record, and persists merged.role. A customer can submit role='support_admin' to promote themselves. JwtStrategy subsequently loads that modified role from the database.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: PATCH /api/users/:id permits users to update their own teamId and organizationId without administrator authorization. Customers can join another organization, and support staff can join another team, gaining access to records protected using those membership fields.

The general profile update accepts data.password and replaces the caller's password without verifying the current password. This bypasses the current-password verification in /api/auth/change-password and lets someone possessing a stolen bearer token establish a new login password.

The user-list query returns all User scalar fields, including passwordHash, and its result is returned directly to the caller. Support agents and team leads can retrieve customer password hashes and hashes of visible teammates for offline cracking. User detail, case-file, and update responses similarly return unfiltered user records.

cwe: CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

extra.message: Directory provisioning fetches the complete user record and logs JSON.stringify(record) on failure, including passwordHash and personal information. The current pushToDirectory implementation always throws, so every successful lookup through the directory-sync endpoint writes these credentials to application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: GET /api/dashboard/activity reads ui_timezone from the request cookie and interpolates it into a SQL string passed to $queryRawUnsafe. An authenticated attacker can terminate the timezone literal and inject SQL to retrieve data outside the intended user-scoped activity query.

The attachment preview builds a shell command containing the uploaded filename and executes it with exec(). Double quotes do not prevent shell substitutions such as $(...). A user can upload a crafted filename to an accessible ticket and request its preview to execute commands as the backend process.

GET /api/exports/tickets/legacy-layout interpolates the report_layout_pref cookie and csvPath query parameter into a command executed with shell:true. Any authenticated staff user can supply shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands, even if the formatting script itself is unavailable.

The administrator-accessible scoring preview passes the decoded formula URL parameter directly to eval(). A support administrator can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the backend process, extending application administration into server code execution and access to process secrets.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code

extra.message: The verified signature download joins the decoded storedName route parameter to privateSignatureDir without checking containment. A caller can supply their own user ID to pass authorization and URL-encoded traversal segments in storedName to read arbitrary files accessible to the backend.

Signature authorization compares the caller with the independently supplied id parameter, but never associates storedName with that user. Uploads place all verified signatures in a shared directory without recording ownership. A user who obtains another signature's storedName can retrieve it by supplying their own ID.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /api/attachments/from-url writes downloaded attacker-controlled bytes using the unrestricted JSON fileName. A filename such as x/../../.env cancels the timestamp-prefixed component during path normalization and escapes uploadDir. Any user with access to a ticket can create or overwrite files outside the upload directory.

The report letterhead endpoint joins the decoded templateName parameter to templatesDir and returns the file contents without a containment check. An authenticated staff user can use URL-encoded ../ segments to read backend configuration, source files, or other readable files.

The mapping-profile endpoint appends .json to the decoded profileName and reads it without enforcing containment in import-profiles. A support administrator can use URL-encoded traversal, such as ../package, to retrieve JSON files outside the approved directory. The .json suffix and JSON.parse restrict the readable file format but do not prevent traversal.

POST /api/replies/macros/shared passes the supplied macroName into path.join and writes the supplied body without a containment check. Staff users can use ../ segments to create or overwrite .txt files outside canned-macros, including verification checklist files.

Checklist generation uses the ticket category's name as a filesystem path without checking containment. Category names are administrator-controlled and may contain ../ segments. Selecting such a category causes the checklist endpoint to read existing .txt files outside verification-checklists or create files there with generated content.

Partner-feed import expands attacker-supplied SYSTEM entity declarations by reading their URI as a local file. A staff user can import a hosted feed declaring an entity for a backend secret file and reference it inside an article body. The file contents are stored in a draft article that the importing user can retrieve.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: POST /api/attachments/from-url fetches the supplied sourceUrl without restricting destinations. An authenticated user with an accessible ticket can request loopback, private-network, or metadata-service URLs. Response bytes are saved as an attachment, allowing the user to retrieve the response.

Both partner and certified feed imports pass the feedUrl query parameter to http.get or https.get without validating the destination. Authenticated staff can make the backend issue requests to internal services. The certified variant's document-type check runs after the request and does not prevent SSRF.

FileInterceptor('file') is configured without upload limits, and the service consumes file.buffer. An authenticated caller can exhaust backend memory with oversized uploads before the service performs ticket authorization. Both signature upload routes have the same interceptor configuration; the verified signature's size check occurs only after buffering.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The from-url attachment flow buffers the entire remote response with arrayBuffer() and then writes it without a byte limit. A user can point sourceUrl to a server returning an arbitrarily large body, exhausting backend memory or upload storage. This remains exploitable with an ordinary public HTTP destination.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Retention relay authorization trusts x-partner-role and the request body's access value. Both routes require only a valid JWT and perform no ticket-scope or partner authentication check. Any customer can name another ticket and forge a retention audit entry attributed to its requester. The verified variant remains vulnerable because the attacker can supply the exact expected string and boolean.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: Dashboard activity applies a user filter only for customers; support agents and team leads receive globally scoped audit records. Both expanded-history variants repeat this omission. These endpoints expose other teams' activity and administrative audit details that AuditService otherwise restricts by ticket assignment or team.

POST /api/tickets/segments/resolve uses only caller-supplied filters and never applies the caller's organization, team, or assignment restrictions. A customer can submit empty filters or target another organization's tickets to retrieve their descriptions, identifiers, and requester information.

POST /api/tickets/segments/named scopes customers but applies no team or assignment restriction to support agents or team leads. Staff can submit empty filters to retrieve tickets across teams, or select an arbitrary teamId, bypassing the normal ticket-access rules.

The ticket handoff endpoint decodes caller-provided JSON, checks access to the original ticket, and writes every merged property except id. Customers can alter protected fields such as requesterId, organizationId, ticketNumber, timestamps, and status. This permits attribution and tenant changes and bypasses the transition checks in the normal update method.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Ticket update checks whether the caller can access the ticket but does not require a staff role for assignment, team, SLA, or status changes. Customers can directly PATCH these operational fields on any ticket in their organization, despite the frontend restricting status controls to staff.

Ticket detail includes complete escalation records for every caller, including customer users. Customers can read internal escalation reasons and resolutions in the API response even though EscalationsService rejects customer reads and the Angular escalation tab is hidden from customers.

cwe: CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

extra.message: Article detail checks only publication status for customers and ignores isPublic. A customer who knows the ID of a published internal article can retrieve its contents, although the listing endpoint explicitly requires isPublic=true. Both bulletin download methods have the same missing visibility check.

Priority-upgrade entitlement is decided using the accountType request-body field rather than the organization's stored plan. A basic-plan customer can submit accountType='enterprise' or 'premium' to obtain an urgent upgrade. The concierge flow demonstrates the intended server-side plan lookup.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: Legacy billing synchronization transmits CRM_API_KEY or the integration secret in an HTTP URL query string. Network observers can capture the credential and ticket identifier, and URL logging can additionally persist the secret. The request explicitly uses unencrypted HTTP.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: CSV exports include customer-controlled ticket subjects and names without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. A customer can store a subject beginning with '=' that is emitted as an active formula when staff open the CSV in spreadsheet software. SLA and escalation exports use the same unprotected serialization pattern.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The handling-note endpoint inserts the request body's note directly into a log message without neutralizing line breaks. Any authenticated user can submit multiline content that creates forged log lines, corrupting the apparent application activity trail.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: Escalation draft handoff validates that status is an enum value but writes it without checking the current state. A staff user with access to an escalation can bypass update()'s transition restrictions, for example moving a requested escalation directly to resolved or reopening a terminal escalation, while also bypassing resolution bookkeeping.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Digest-cadence tokens contain a user sub and are signed for seven days using the same secret as login tokens. JwtStrategy accepts tokens using that secret and sub without checking audience or token purpose. Anyone possessing a cadence-confirmation token can therefore use it as a bearer token for the user's full API privileges.

Legal-hold and archived attachment encryption derive their key from a public hardcoded string when RETENTION_SEAL_KEY is unset. Anyone obtaining the stored ciphertext can derive the identical key and decrypt the files, defeating their at-rest confidentiality.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Payment verification references are encrypted using a key derived from the public fallback 'change-me-in-vault' and a fixed salt when NOTES_SEAL_KEY is absent. The resulting ciphertext, IV, and authentication tag are stored together in note content, so anyone with those notes can derive the key and recover the protected references.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The runtime customer-import endpoint assigns the known password 'Welcome123!' whenever a row omits password. Imported accounts are immediately usable and have no mandatory password-change state. An attacker who knows an imported email address can authenticate using this shared default.

The successor-promotion confirmation guard validates the workbench cookie and change token but never compares the session's userId with the JWT-authenticated user. Someone holding an administrator bearer token can satisfy the additional identity-confirmation requirement using a workbench session obtained with their own lower-privileged credentials.

The authenticated route-to-desk endpoint passes the destination request-body field directly to res.redirect(). The service checks escalation access but does not validate the destination, so arbitrary external URLs are accepted as redirect targets.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
